vit-nau-khom.name: Mekong Delta Duck and Pineapple Soup
aliases: Duck Soup with Coconut Water and Pineapple
vit-nau-khom.description: Duck simmers with pineapple, straw mushrooms, carrot and coconut water. Its gently sweet and tart broth is served with rice noodles for a comforting family meal.
vit-nau-khom.finished_dish: Tender duck pieces stay intact in a clear, lightly sweet broth with pineapple, carrot and mushrooms.
vit-nau-khom.serving: Ladle into bowls, finish with cilantro and serve hot with fresh rice noodles or wheat noodles.
tips: Rub the duck with salt and ginger or a little rice wine, then rinse well to reduce its strong aroma.
Briefly saute the carrot and pineapple first so they hold their shape during simmering.
Cooking time depends on the duck; check that the meat is fully cooked before serving.
search_terms: duck soup served with rice noodles
vit-nau-khom.image_alt: A bowl of Vietnamese duck and pineapple soup with duck pieces, pineapple, carrot and straw mushrooms in broth.

ingredients.name: Pineapple
ingredients.notes: Mince part of it and cut the rest into chunks.

ingredients.name: Carrot
ingredients.notes: Peel and cut into thick rounds.

ingredients.name: Dried wood ear mushrooms
ingredients.notes: Soak until rehydrated and trim the tough base.

ingredients.name: Cooking oil
ingredients.notes: For sauteing and frying the aromatics.

preparation_steps: Rub the duck with salt and ginger or a little rice wine, rinse well and cut into serving pieces. Marinate with chili sauce, a little salt, sugar and seasoning powder for about 15 minutes.
Soak the wood ear mushrooms until soft and cut them; clean the straw mushrooms. Cut the pineapple, mince some of it, and slice the carrot and onion.
Bruise the lemongrass and mince the garlic and shallot. Keep the minced pineapple separate from the chunks.
cooking_steps: Heat a little oil and saute the carrot until just tender; remove it. Briefly saute the pineapple chunks until fragrant and set aside.

Fry the garlic and shallot until fragrant, add the duck and cook until the surface firms. Stir in the minced pineapple and wood ear mushrooms, then add coconut water and lemongrass. Bring to a boil and skim the foam.

Lower the heat and simmer with the straw mushrooms for about 25 minutes. Add the carrot and pineapple chunks and cook until the duck is tender and fully cooked. Adjust the salt, sugar and seasoning powder.
Add the onion and cilantro at the end. Serve hot with fresh rice noodles or wheat noodles.
vit-nau-khom.media_alt_text: Duck simmered with pineapple, carrot and straw mushrooms in a light broth, served in a blue-and-white bowl.

ngan-nuong-ngu-vi.name: Vietnamese Five-Spice Roasted Muscovy Duck
ngan-nuong-ngu-vi.description: Muscovy duck is coated with five-spice, oyster sauce and honey, then roasted until fragrant and browned. Serve it with herbs and hot rice for a relaxed family meal.
ngan-nuong-ngu-vi.finished_dish: The skin is evenly browned and fragrant with five-spice; the meat is cooked through, tender and moist.
ngan-nuong-ngu-vi.serving: Rest briefly, chop into portions and serve hot with fresh herbs and lime-pepper salt.
tips: After rubbing the duck with salt and vinegar, rinse it well so it is not overly salty.
Marinate thoroughly and turn the duck during roasting for even browning.
Use a food thermometer to check that the thickest breast and thigh portions reach at least 74°C (165°F).
ngan-nuong-ngu-vi.image_alt: Vietnamese five-spice roasted Muscovy duck with glossy golden-brown skin, served on a plate with herbs.

ingredients.name: Cleaned whole Muscovy duck
ingredients.notes: Choose a medium-sized duck and drain well.

ingredients.name: Chili powder
ingredients.notes: Adjust for the preferred heat level.

ingredients.name: Honey
ingredients.notes: Adds color and a mild sweetness to the skin.

ingredients.name: Salt
ingredients.notes: Rub over the duck during cleaning; rinse off before marinating.

ingredients.name: Vinegar
ingredients.notes: Use with salt to clean the duck; do not add to the marinade.

preparation_steps: Remove any remaining pin feathers. Rub the duck with salt and vinegar, rinse several times and drain thoroughly.
Mix the chili powder, five-spice powder, oyster sauce and honey. Rub the seasoning over the outside and inside of the duck and marinate for at least 30 minutes.
cooking_steps: Preheat an oven to 180°C or prepare a bed of glowing charcoal. Roast the duck, turning it so all sides cook evenly. If using an oven, brush with a little marinade as needed to prevent the skin from drying.
Roast until the skin is golden brown and the thickest breast and thigh portions reach at least 74°C (165°F); timing varies with the bird's size and the equipment.
Rest the duck for a few minutes, chop into portions and serve with herbs and lime-pepper salt.
ngan-nuong-ngu-vi.media_alt_text: Whole five-spice roasted Muscovy duck with crisp golden-brown skin, served on a ceramic platter.

me-ga-kho-thom.name: Vietnamese Chicken Gizzards Braised with Pineapple
aliases: Chicken Gizzards with Pineapple and Coconut Water
me-ga-kho-thom.serving_basis: A pan for four people, served with rice.
me-ga-kho-thom.description: Chicken gizzards are quickly braised with pineapple, ginger and coconut water. The gentle sweet-sour seasoning makes this a hearty everyday rice dish.
me-ga-kho-thom.finished_dish: The gizzards are tender with a light bite, the pineapple holds its shape and the braising sauce lightly coats each piece.
me-ga-kho-thom.serving: Serve hot with steamed rice, sliced scallions and ground black pepper.
tips: Scrape away the yellow inner lining and wash the gizzards thoroughly with salt or vinegar.
Score the gizzards shallowly so they absorb seasoning more quickly.
Add the pineapple after the gizzards have browned, then braise just until tender so the fruit does not collapse.
search_terms: Vietnamese chicken gizzards braised with pineapple
chicken gizzards braised in coconut water
me-ga-kho-thom.image_alt: Vietnamese chicken gizzards braised with pineapple and aromatics in a lightly glossy sauce.

ingredients.name: Chicken gizzards
ingredients.notes: Clean the yellow lining, rinse thoroughly and cut into bite-size pieces.

ingredients.name: Shallots
ingredients.notes: Mince some and leave small bulbs whole if available.

ingredients.name: Chili sauce
ingredients.notes: Reduce or omit for a milder dish.

ingredients.name: Seasoning powder
ingredients.notes: Use for the marinade and adjust the sauce to taste.

ingredients.name: Salt
ingredients.notes: Rub over the gizzards during cleaning, then rinse off.

preparation_steps: Rub the gizzards with salt, rinse several times, scrape away the yellow lining and cut into bite-size pieces. Lightly score the surface so the seasoning can penetrate.
Cut the pineapple, mince the garlic and some shallot, slice the ginger, bruise the chili and cut the scallions.
Marinate the gizzards with soy sauce, chili sauce, seasoning powder, pepper, garlic and shallot for about 10 minutes.
cooking_steps: Fry the remaining shallot, garlic and ginger until fragrant. Add the marinated gizzards and stir over medium heat until they firm up.
Add the pineapple and stir for a few minutes, then pour in the coconut water. Add whole shallots and chili, lower the heat and braise until the gizzards are cooked and the sauce lightly thickens.
Taste and adjust the seasoning. Stir in the scallions briefly, turn off the heat and serve hot with rice.
me-ga-kho-thom.media_alt_text: Chicken gizzards braised with golden pineapple, shiitake mushrooms and scallions on a blue-and-white plate.

vit-nuong-chao.name: Southern Vietnamese Duck Roasted with Fermented Tofu
aliases: Vietnamese Duck Roasted with Fermented tofu
vit-nuong-chao.description: Duck is marinated in fermented tofu with lemongrass, garlic and ginger, then roasted in an air fryer. The skin turns fragrant and golden while the meat stays tender and savory.
vit-nuong-chao.finished_dish: The duck is tender inside with golden-brown skin and a fragrant coating of fermented tofu, lemongrass and ginger.
vit-nuong-chao.serving: Serve hot with steamed rice, rice noodles or fresh herbs.
tips: Score the skin shallowly so the marinade adheres evenly.
Use less fermented tofu liquid or chili paste for a milder flavor.
Turn the duck halfway through cooking, brush with a little sauce and check that it is fully cooked.
search_terms: Vietnamese duck roasted with fermented tofu
vit-nuong-chao.image_alt: Southern Vietnamese duck roasted with fermented tofu, lemongrass and ginger, with a golden-brown surface.

ingredients.name: Duck meat
ingredients.notes: Cut into thick pieces about 5 cm across.

ingredients.name: Fermented tofu cubes
ingredients.notes: Mash with the fermented tofu liquid.

ingredients.name: Ginger
ingredients.notes: Use some crushed for cleaning and mince the rest.

ingredients.name: Salt
ingredients.notes: Rub over the duck while cleaning, then rinse off.

ingredients.name: Vinegar
ingredients.notes: Use a little for cleaning, then rinse off.

ingredients.name: Rice wine
ingredients.notes: Use with ginger while cleaning the duck.

preparation_steps: Rub the duck with salt, vinegar and crushed ginger, rinse well and drain. Cut into thick pieces about 5 cm across.
Mince the shallot, garlic and lemongrass. Mash the fermented tofu with its liquid and mix with ginger, chili paste, soy sauce, five-spice powder, sugar and seasoning powder.
Coat the duck with the marinade and chill for at least 30 minutes; marinate longer if time allows.
cooking_steps: Preheat the air fryer to 180°C for 5 minutes. Arrange the duck in one layer with the skin facing down.
Roast at 150°C for about 15 minutes, turn skin-side up and brush with a little more marinade. Roast at 180°C for about 10 minutes.
Check that the thickest piece reaches at least 74°C (165°F). If needed, cook in additional 5-minute intervals. Serve hot with noodles or rice.
vit-nuong-chao.media_alt_text: Sliced fermented-tofu-marinated duck with lightly glossy golden-brown skin, arranged on a blue-and-white plate.

ga-xao-bap-cai.name: Vietnamese Chicken and Cabbage Stir-Fry
aliases: Vietnamese Chicken Cabbage Stir-Fry for Rice
ga-xao-bap-cai.description: Tender chicken thigh is quickly stir-fried with crisp-tender cabbage and a light soy-based sauce. It is a practical everyday dish served with hot rice.
ga-xao-bap-cai.finished_dish: The chicken is juicy and fully cooked, the cabbage stays pleasantly crisp, and a light glossy sauce coats the ingredients.
ga-xao-bap-cai.serving: Serve immediately while hot, topped with scallions.
tips: Cut the chicken into even pieces so they cook at the same rate.
Mix the soy sauce, oyster sauce, water and cornstarch before heating the pan.
Add the cabbage after the chicken has browned so the vegetables do not become limp.
ga-xao-bap-cai.image_alt: Vietnamese chicken and cabbage stir-fry with juicy chicken pieces and crisp cabbage in a light glossy sauce.

ingredients.name: Boneless chicken thighs
ingredients.notes: Remove the skin and cut into bite-size pieces.

ingredients.name: Cabbage
ingredients.notes: Remove the core and cut into bite-size pieces.

ingredients.name: Water
ingredients.notes: Whisk with the soy and oyster sauces.

ingredients.name: Cornstarch
ingredients.notes: Dissolve in the sauce before cooking.

preparation_steps: Cut the chicken into evenly sized pieces and marinate with salt and pepper for about 10 minutes.
Cut the cabbage into bite-size pieces, rinse and drain; finely slice the scallions.
Whisk the soy sauce, oyster sauce, water and cornstarch until smooth.
cooking_steps: Heat the oil in a pan, briefly stir-fry the scallions until fragrant, then add the chicken. Stir-fry over high heat for about 3 minutes until the surface firms.
Add the cabbage and stir-fry for about 3 minutes.
Pour in the sauce and toss until it thickens lightly and coats the ingredients. Check that the thickest chicken pieces are fully cooked and reach at least 74°C (165°F), then remove from the heat.
ga-xao-bap-cai.media_alt_text: Chicken stir-fried with white and green cabbage and scallions on a ceramic plate.
